study_identification_part.si4_title: Personalizing progressive changes to brain structure in Alzheimer's disease using normative modeling

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study applied neuroanatomical normative modeling to serial MRI data to quantify regional brain structural changes as Alzheimer's disease (AD) progresses, aiming to track disease trajectories, predict MCI to AD progression, and relate these markers to other AD indicators.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear models (adjusted for age, sex, AC score) for comparing rate of change in tOC between diagnostic groups; Linear mixed models (unconditional, with random intercept for individual participants) for individual trajectories of tOC over time; Cox proportional hazards regression for MCI to AD progression risk based on tOC change (Kaplan-Meier plots for illustration); Linear regression (adjusted for age, sex, years of education) for relationships between tOC rate of change and cognitive composite scores (memory, executive function), and interactions; Linear regression (adjusted for age, sex) for relationships between tOC rate of change and amyloid/tau PET markers, and interactions; ANOVA (adjusted for age, sex) for differences in tOC rate of change by APOE ε 4 status, and interactions; Linear regression (adjusted for age, sex, APOE ε 4 status) for relationships between PRS and tOC rate of change, and interactions.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Neuroanatomical normative modeling applied to serial MRI data revealed that total outlier count (tOC) increased in AD and MCI converters, correlated with non-imaging markers, and predicted MCI to AD progression, with the hippocampus showing the highest rate of change, supporting tOC and brain outlier maps as personalized markers for AD patients and MCI progression risk.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: In AD patients, the left hippocampus consistently showed the highest proportion of outliers, increasing from 47% at baseline to 72% at 24 months. Overall, AD patients exhibited a greater number of 'rate of z score change' outliers, with the left hippocampus reaching 53%. Total outlier count (tOC) significantly increased over time in the AD group (β = 0.38, p = 9.8 × 10^-13) and MCI group (β = 0.001, p = 0.004), but not in controls. The rate of tOC change was highest in AD (mean = 5.26, SD = 9.85) and intermediate in MCI (mean = 0.59, SD = 4.57). MCI progressive individuals had a significantly higher rate of tOC change (mean = 3.97, SD = 11.27) than MCI stable (mean = 0.53, SD = 4.61), with an increase of three outliers in the first 12 months elevating the risk of progression from MCI to AD by 30.2% (HR = 1.09, 95% CI: [1.06, 1.12], p = 1.4 × 10^-14). The rate of tOC change also correlated significantly with poorer memory (β = -1.99, p = 2.0 × 10^-16), executive function (β = -1.77, p = 2.0 × 10^-16), increased amyloid PET SUVR (β = 0.006, p = 0.001), and tau PET SUVR (β = 0.03, p = 0.0001), and was associated with APOE ε 4 homozygosity (β = 2.33, p = 0.003) and heterozygosity (β = 5.77, p = 0.018).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The reference dataset is over-representative of European ancestry and ADNI participants are primarily in early/intermediate AD stages with fewer comorbidities, limiting generalizability. Within-subject noise in longitudinal data and varying FreeSurfer versions (5 & 6) in ADNI data may introduce inconsistencies. The model treats brain regions independently despite likely intercorrelations.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Although our reference dataset is large, it is over-representative of European ancestry... ADNI participants are more likely to be in the early to intermediate stages of AD, and less likely to have comorbidities... some within-subject noise remains in longitudinal data... ADNI data were processed with a variety of FreeSurfer versions (5 & 6)... our model treats brain regions independently

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Provides region-level information and mapped outlier scores for personalized brain health assessment; has potential utility in detecting MCI progression to AD dementia for clinical decision-making; the approach does not require access to raw scans, offering open-access scripts for z-scores, tOC, and outlier maps, facilitating clinical translation; potential to aid AD therapeutic trials by stratifying participants based on atrophy patterns and serving as a personalized outcome measure to increase power and sensitivity.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study was conducted 'for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI)'. Data from ADNI were used, and ADNI investigators contributed to data collection but not analysis or writing of this report.
